meta.studentProfile: one-to-one adult or teen English learner
meta.communicativeGoal: Talk about the movie Luca: describe characters, discuss themes of friendship and freedom, and express opinions using gerund and infinitive forms.

controls.title: Time to Read!
paragraphs: Luca is a young sea monster. He lives under the sea near the Italian coast. He spends his days taking care of fish. But Luca is curious about the world above the surface.
One day, Luca meets Alberto. Alberto is also a sea monster, but he has a secret. He lives on land and pretends to be a human boy. Alberto shows Luca that sea monsters can transform when they are dry.
Luca and Alberto become friends. Luca decides to escape from his underwater life. Together, they explore the human town. They want to buy a Vespa and enjoy freedom together.
But the boys must hide their true identity. Water can make them transform back into sea monsters. Luca's parents are looking for him. The boys decide to enter a race to win money.

Luca meets Giulia, a human girl. She becomes his friend too. Luca starts to enjoy learning new things. In the end, Luca's parents learn to accept his dreams. The story is about friendship, freedom, and accepting who you are.

cards.title: Gerund (-ing form)
cards.body: We use the gerund (verb + -ing) after certain verbs: enjoy, finish, avoid, keep, suggest. We also use the gerund after prepositions like of, in, on, at, about.
examples: Luca enjoys swimming in the sea.
He keeps dreaming about the surface.
The boys dream of traveling on a Vespa.

cards.title: Infinitive (to + verb)
cards.body: We use the infinitive (to + base verb) after verbs like: want, decide, plan, hope, agree, learn, need.
examples: Luca wants to explore the town.

cards.title: Same meaning: gerund and infinitive
cards.body: After some verbs like like, love, hate, start, begin, we can use both the gerund and the infinitive. The meaning is the same.
examples: Luca started exploring the town. = Luca started to explore the town.
Luca loves swimming. = Luca loves to swim.

cards.title: Prepositions + gerund
cards.body: After a preposition (in, on, at, of, about, for, with), we always use the gerund (-ing form). We never use the infinitive after a preposition.

lessonFlow: Greet the student and chat briefly about animated movies. Ask if they have seen Luca.
Do the Warm Up word association. Keep it fast — about 5 minutes.
Lead-In opinion sort: encourage the student to explain each choice. Spend 8-10 minutes.
Target Vocabulary: do the definition match first, then gap fill. Drill pronunciation. 10 minutes.
Reading: student reads aloud. Check understanding with the quiz. Discuss unknown words. 10 minutes.
Grammar: present the gerund vs infinitive rules using the rule cards. Then complete the rule and choose correct. 8-10 minutes.
Grammar Practice: controlled input and dropdown choice. Let the student self-correct. 8 minutes.
Speaking: use the questions for free conversation. Do translation self-check if time allows. 5-8 minutes.
Wrap up: review key vocabulary and grammar. Assign optional homework from resources.
adaptationNotes: For a weaker student: skip the translation self-check and spend more time on the gap fill and controlled input practice.
For a stronger student: ask the student to retell the Luca story using all 10 target vocabulary words. Add more speaking questions about the themes.
If the student has not seen Luca: spend 2 minutes describing the basic plot before the reading section. Show a short trailer if available.
If time is short: reduce speaking to 3 questions and skip translation.
For teen learners: focus more on the friendship and adventure themes. For adults: discuss the parent-child relationship and freedom themes more deeply.
answerKeySummary: Definition match: sea monster = magical creature that lives under the sea; surface = top part of water; transform = change how you look; curious = wanting to learn; hide = be where nobody can see you; escape = get away from a place; explore = look around a new place; pretend = act like something is true; secret = something you don't want others to know; freedom = doing what you want.
Gap fill answers: sea monster, curious, hide, explore, transform, secret, pretend, escape, surface, freedom.
Reading quiz: 1) Under the sea, 2) Alberto, 3) A Vespa, 4) They transform back, 5) A sea monster's adventure.
Complete the rule: 1) gerund, 2) infinitive, 3) gerund, 4) gerund or infinitive, 5) infinitive.
Choose correct: 1) swimming, 2) to buy, 3) going, 4) to tell, 5) being, 6) to help.
Controlled input: 1) swimming, 2) to explore, 3) going, 4) to enter, 5) traveling, 6) learning/to learn, 7) crying/to cry, 8) to win.
Dropdown choice: 1) eating, 2) to stay, 3) telling, 4) to win, 5) talking, 6) to escape, 7) hiding, 8) to help.
